b081:
Dopamine Receptor Burnout / DAWS Pattern: Uridine Monophosphate

Who this is for: Uridine isn't for everyone with depression. It could be helpful, though, for folks that show a "burned-out dopamine receptor" pattern, where everything feels gray and there's no desire for anything (anhedonia). These folks also find that dreams and psychedelic visuals are weak, so they need unusually high doses to feel anything, and as a result they tend to compulsively reach for ketamine/LSD/novelty just to get a hit. In the medical literature, this burnout pattern is talked about with regard to dopamine agonist withdrawal syndrome (DAWS). People with DAWS, after tapering off dopamine agonist drugs, present with symptoms of anxiety, panic, dysphoria, depression, agitation, fatigue, autonomic symptoms, pain, and drug cravings. Scott's case looked like DAWS with dopamine receptor D2/D3 reward-system downregulation, which then got worse from frequent LSD microdosing and from trying to force dopamine hits with ketamine.

Dopamine Receptor Burnout / DAWS Pattern: Uridine Monophosphate

Who this is for: Uridine isn't for everyone with depression. It could be helpful, though, for folks that show a "burned-out dopamine receptor" pattern, where everything feels gray and there's no desire for anything (anhedonia). These folks also find that dreams and psychedelic visuals are weak, so they need unusually high doses to feel anything, and as a result they tend to compulsively reach for ketamine/LSD/novelty just to get a hit. In the medical literature, this burnout pattern is talked about with regard to dopamine agonist withdrawal syndrome (DAWS). People with DAWS, after tapering off dopamine agonist drugs (like pramipexole or ropinirole), present with symptoms of anxiety, panic, dysphoria, depression, agitation, fatigue, autonomic symptoms, pain, and drug cravings. Scott's case looked like DAWS with dopamine receptor D2/D3 reward-system downregulation, which then got worse from frequent LSD microdosing and from trying to force dopamine hits with ketamine.
b082: The tool: Uridine monophosphate (UMP). There's no study showing that "UMP cures DAWS", so the best evidence we have is more basic than that. Uridine, choline, and DHA are circulating precursors (building blocks carried in the blood) for brain phosphatide / synaptic membrane synthesis, that is, for making the fatty membranes at the connections between neurons. Wurtman's group has shown that DHA + uridine + choline can increase synaptic membrane components and synaptic proteins, that DHA-induced dendritic spine formation is enhanced by UMP in animals (the spines are the tiny bumps on neurons where connections form), and that dietary UMP increased potassium-evoked dopamine release and neurite outgrowth in aged rats (old rats that got UMP in their food released more dopamine and grew more nerve fibers). So the mechanism is plausible, but the DAWS use is still a cautious human extrapolation (applying the animal findings to people) plus anecdote.
b083: Scott's signal: Scott was already getting choline from eggs and DHA/EPA (the omega-3s) from fish oil. Within a day of adding a standard dose of UMP, though, he noticed a striking difference. His dreams got vivid again, and real childhood memories started coming back in them. His psychedelic tolerance seemed to drop, and his ketamine/LSD cravings fell off hard. We can't tell from this whether UMP actually rebuilt his D3 receptors (one of the dopamine receptor types) overnight. But in the right person, a response like that can be a very clear sign that the synaptic-membrane / dopamine-receptor-recovery axis (the system that keeps rebuilding the membranes and dopamine receptors where neurons connect) was starved.
